name: Me When Median Problem
description: You are given two arrays of positive integers $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, both of length $$$n$$$. You will perform the following operation exactly $$$n - 1$$$ times: let $$$m$$$ be the current length of $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, note that the lengths will always be equal. select an integer $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \le i \lt m$$$): let $$$S$$$ be the multiset $$$\{a_i, a_{i + 1}, b_i, b_{i + 1}\}$$$ sort the elements of $$$S$$$ such that $$$s_1 \le s_2 \le s_3 \le s_4$$$. now replace $$$a_i, a_{i + 1}$$$ with $$$s_2$$$ and $$$b_i, b_{i + 1}$$$ with $$$s_3$$$. More formally, replace $$$a$$$ with $$$[a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{i - 1},s_2,a_{i + 2},\ldots,a_m]$$$, and replace $$$b$$$ with $$$[b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_{i - 1},s_3,b_{i + 2},\ldots,b_m]$$$. After performing all operations, there will be exactly $$$1$$$ element remaining in both $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$. Determine the maximum value of $$$\min(a_1, b_1)$$$ attainable if you perform operations optimally.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each testcase contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$) — the length of the arrays $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$. The second line of each testcase contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{n}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 2 \cdot n$$$). The third line of each testcase contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_{n}$$$ ($$$1 \le b_i \le 2 \cdot n$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each testcase, output the maximum value of $$$\min(a_1,b_1)$$$ attainable.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2229D — Me When Median Problem [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
